newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds start quiet with weather the focus.
newsitem.headline: European feeds start quiet with weather the focus.

text.p: European feeds made the usual quiet start to trade on Monday focusing on weather developments in the United States and central Europe.

Physical sellers offered soyabeanmeal at mixed levels from Friday, with nearby prices up to three dollars higher and others down around two. The changing weather fortunes of the Chicago futures market continued to hamper business here, traders said.
"First we had forecasts of hot, dry weather and then rain. You can see that reflected in Project A trade," one said.
There were no trades reported in early European business.
Traders said it was still too early to predict any impact from the flooding in central Europe, where Poland's rapeseed crop was seen as being particularly affected.

The crop, already damaged by the severe winter, is predicted to drop by a 100,000 tonnes to between 300,000 and 350,000 as a result of the floods. But the impact of a shortfall is expected to be compensated by good harvests elsewhere in Europe.
"We haven't got any precise figures yet, but I don't see a big impact. The EU crop is pretty large," said one trader.
